context: A screenshot of ghent-live, a 3D map of the historic centre of Ghent (Belgium) rendered in a web browser, shown on a projector during a talk. The app draws its controls over the scene: camera preset buttons, a day/night switch, layer switches and name labels on landmarks.

checks.name: preset_buttons
checks.instructions: A row of buttons along the bottom of the screen names camera views, among them 'From above' and 'Street level'.

checks.name: light_and_layers
checks.instructions: A panel on the left, under the title, holds a Day/Night switch and a list of layer switches (for example 'Buildings').

checks.name: landmark_labels
checks.instructions: Labels naming Ghent landmarks (for example 'Belfort', 'Sint-Baafs' or 'Gravensteen') are placed over the 3D scene.

checks.name: title_clear
checks.instructions: The title 'Ghent, live' in the top-left corner is fully visible, not covered by any button, panel or label.

checks.name: no_overlap
checks.instructions: No two labels, buttons or panels overlap each other.

checks.name: stage_readability
checks.instructions: The on-screen text is readable from the back of a room. How readable is the on-screen text when the screen is projected for an audience of 100 people?
